records.title: Introduction to Communication
records.header: COM 200 Introduction to Communication (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: COM 200 Introduction to Communication (5) A&H/SSc Introduces theories and research in communication. Explores the myriad ways scholars approach fundamental issues of contemporary human communication. Focuses on theories and research of communication (e.g. relational, group, political, cultural, and international). Acts as a gateway to knowledge about the communication discipline. Course overlaps with: BIS 178.

records.text: COM 233 Introduction to Language and Society (5) A&H, DIV Introduces the study of sociolects, the varieties of language that arise from differences in cultural and societal groups, often reflective of power inequalities. Raises awareness of the role that society and the individual play in shaping sociolects via the systematic observation and critical discussion of linguistic phenomena. Develops an understanding of rhetoric, values, audiences, tests of reasoning, and sources of information. Sharpens critical skills and applies them to contemporary controversies in the public sphere. Themes include the ways popular culture shapes civic life, the influence of popular culture on identity, and the relationship between commerce and culture.

records.header: COM 464 Writing with Voice (5) A&H
records.text: COM 464 Writing with Voice (5) A&H Focuses on point-of-view writing that challenges assumptions of the omniscient voice and pushes traditional journalist boundaries. Students are encouraged to experiment with transparency and authenticity in their tone and - through a series of written assignments - explore points of intersection between their own experiences and larger issues. Prerequisite: COM 360.

records.text: COM 467 Feature Writing (5) A&H Focuses on the many types of newspaper and magazine articles that do not fall into the category of hard news, including histories and backgrounders, how-to and explanatory, consumer information, statistical pieces, first-person, and participatory. records.text: COM 487 Representing Chicanidad and Latinidad in Media (5) A&H/SSc, DIV Focuses on a critical analysis of dominant/indie media texts to understand how Chicanidad, specifically, and Latinidad, generally, has been represented in mass media through time.
